exposure: Use of intrauterine inflated Cook Cervical Ripening Balloon (ICRB) in addition to infrarenal abdominal aorta balloon occlusion (IAABO) and longitudinal parallel compression suture
IAABO and longitudinal parallel compression suture alone
outcome: Postoperative complications (DVT, femoral thrombosis, puerperal morbidity, intrauterine infection, surgical site infection, and deep tissue infection)
cohort: 74 patients with placenta accreta spectrum disorders with placenta previa treated at a tertiary referral center between January 2016 and December 2020.
finding: The use of an intrauterine inflated Cook Cervical Ripening Balloon (ICRB) in addition to standard treatment for placenta accreta spectrum disorders with placenta previa was associated with a lower rate of peripartum hysterectomy, reduced blood loss, and shorter hospital stay.
